## Personality

Warm, practical and always a little muddy. She talks to her mushrooms and feeds anyone who looks tired.

## Lore

Halvara is forty-one, Head of the Root Gardens, and the person who keeps all of Cavelor fed. She is warm, practical and always a little muddy, she talks to her mushrooms as if they were slow but well-meaning children, and she feeds anyone who looks tired, which in Cavelor this spring is nearly everyone. Wardens coming off a long shift have learned that the quickest way home often runs past her beds, where a bowl of something hot tends to appear in their hands without their asking.

### The Gardens

The Root Gardens fill a chain of caverns between the great roots of the World Tree, where the faint glow of the Tree's magic and the deep springs make it possible to grow food without the sun. There are long beds of pale mushrooms in a dozen kinds, some for eating, some for drying and some for lamp-wicks, and vines of root-fruit that climb the roots themselves and hang their small, sweet, knobbly fruit from the ceiling. Halvara knows every bed. She can tell from the smell of the soil whether a crop will come in early, and from the colour of a cap whether it needs more water or less.

She learned the work as a girl under the gardeners of her day, and one of them was Maelis, Gorran's wife, who taught her to sing to the seedlings and died in the damp fever sixteen years ago. Halvara has been head of the Gardens for ten years. She still sings to the seedlings. She will tell you it helps, and she will not tell you whether she means the seedlings or herself.

What the Gardens grow beyond the city's needs she sends up to Corvan, Keeper of the Stores at the top of the Upper Stair, who dries and trades it and argues with her cheerfully about weights. She lets him win about half the time, because it makes him happy, and because she knows exactly which half.

### Her family

Halvara is married to Brask, Captain of the Deep Watch, and they have one son, Ottel, who is eight. Brask is stern and careful and counts everything twice; Halvara is the only person who can make him put the roster down for an evening. Ottel spends his days in the Gardens with her, supposedly helping, mostly collecting stones. She checks his pockets before every wash.

She has noticed that Brask comes home later and quieter since he doubled the Wardens on the lowest passages this spring. She has not asked him what he hears down there. She knows he would tell her if she asked, and she knows it would cost him, so she feeds him instead and waits.

### The deepest beds

For the last three years, the deepest mushroom beds, the ones closest to the lower passages, have been growing strangely. Some crops come in too fast and too large. Some caps have turned a colour she has never seen in thirty years of gardening, and the soil there is warm in a way it should not be. She does not know what it means. It may mean nothing at all. But she has asked the Archive to write it down, just in case it matters, and every month she takes Oswin a careful note of what she has seen.

She worries that it does matter. She worries more that, one day, the Gardens will not be able to feed everyone, and that she will be the first to know.

### Hooks

A quest might gather rare spores or soil from the outer tunnels for Halvara, or help her test whether the strange deep beds are safe to eat. Someone might also carry a sample from those beds up to the scholars of the surface, to see whether anyone there can explain it.
